applies_why: The judge text gives UNDERDETERMINED because a cited verse does not name whose body is the channel, i.e. does not state the link or its contrary.
quote: the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: 'single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for ... UNDERDETERMINED'—whether it bars an UNDERDETERMINED resting on a verse's silence ('without naming whose body') or only bars treating such silence as conclusive for one side.
why: The judge's stated reason for UNDERDETERMINED is that Acts 2:30 leaves whose body is the channel unnamed, which is precisely using a single verse's not stating the link or its contrary as a ground for UNDERDETERMINED.
